newsitem.title: POLAND: All Polish 15 NFIs complete issue prospectuses.
newsitem.headline: All Polish 15 NFIs complete issue prospectuses.

text.p: All 15 National Investment Funds in Poland's mass privatisation programme have completed their issue prospectuses, bringing them closer to their planned flotation in 1997, a deputy treasury minister said on Monday.
Wieslaw Kaczmarek told a news conference the prospectuses of the now state-owned funds (NFI) would now be sent to the Securities Commission (KPW) for clearance.

The KPW's approval would pave the way for the exchange of 25.7 million privatisation certificates, bought by adult Poles over the last 12 months, for a share in each of the funds and their bourse trade.
"Today I signed the final issue prospectus -- fund No. 12 -- so all 15 National Investment Fund prospectuses have been signed by a representative of the state treasury," Kaczmarek said.
The KPW said last Thursday that it had already received three of the prospectuses.
Kaczmarek said the ministry, which oversees the NFI programme, had kept to its goal to finish its work on the prospectuses by December 9.
The ministry expects the funds to reach the bourse in the first half of 1997.
Under the government programme, each fund was given control of about 33 medium-sized companies and minority stakes in 479 firms.
Kaczmarek also said 20 to 30 firms grouped in the funds could reach Poland's nascent over-the-counter market by the end of next year.
The market's president, Czeslaw Gawlowski, has said up to 30 NFI firms could enter the market by the end of first half 1997. The market started trade with one firm on Friday.
